group_assessment.counts_measured: PubMed esearch 2026-10-02: 'Hsu LJ[au]' 103, 'Hsu LJ[au] AND WWOX' 30. The unqualified count is inflated by author-name ambiguity and is not used for weighting.
group_assessment.weighting: Hsu and Chang at National Cheng Kung University — one of the two founding WWOX laboratories, working on their own knockout line. Primary for the gene; the disease studied here is skin homeostasis, not WWOX-DEE. NOT INDEPENDENT of PMID 37897534 in this wave: same senior author, same mouse line.
group_assessment.note: Li-Jin Hsu and Nan-Shan Chang, National Cheng Kung University -- one of the two founding WWOX laboratories, and the same senior author as PMID 37897534 in this wave. These two records are NOT independent of each other. The Wwox knockout line is the group's own.

field_density.note: High WWOX density and high measurement density: knockout mice with a heterozygous arm carried throughout, primary keratinocytes, HaCaT knockdown, histology, TEM, flow cytometry, corneometry and fibre-optic thermometry. 323 WWOX/Wwox mentions in the JATS.

multihop.enumeration_method: <ref> elements counted in the JATS: 75. Not classified by gene-directedness.
multihop.note: ONE HOP QUEUED BY NAME: Nowakowska et al. 2014 (HT29 colon adenocarcinoma, raised WWOX increasing proliferation). It is the second independent instance of added WWOX doing the opposite of the tumour-suppressor expectation, and it is carried here only as this paper's citation of it.

corpus_crossquery.query: Is there an existing pharmacodynamic-marker candidate for WWOX, and would pERK qualify under section 13?
corpus_crossquery.finding: No candidate exists, and pERK does not qualify as a disease biomarker: it is a Tier 2-shaped readout by position in the pathway but it reports hundreds of upstream inputs, it was measured here by immunohistochemistry in mouse skin of a constitutive null, and the direction (reduced) is the ordinary consequence of reduced proliferation. Recorded as a rejected candidate with its reason.

retraction_check.result: No retraction, no expression of concern, no erratum. Article type 'Journal Article'.

flagged.citing_relation: citation only. Fabbri 2005 is cited once, in the Discussion, inside a list of papers supporting the sentence that WWOX overexpression suppresses growth in malignant cells. It supplies no reagent, no method and no data to PMID 33195192, and nothing this reading carries from PMID 33195192 depends on it. ALREADY HELD BY THE MODEL: the same source is PAPER 082, status background_only, Integrity status PUBLICATION_INTEGRITY_HOLD, deliberately linked to no claim; the expression of concern (PMID 28373548) is narrow in scope -- one beta-actin panel in Figure 1B -- and is not a retraction. This screen rediscovered independently what the registry already records, and changes nothing.

entries.proposition: THE PHARMACODYNAMIC READOUT THE ASSIGNMENT ASKED ABOUT, WITH ITS EXACT SCOPE: it is pERK AND total ERK, in mouse epidermal keratinocytes of a constitutive whole-body null, by immunohistochemistry.
entries.snippet: keratinocytes expressed significantly reduced levels of pERK and total ERK1/2 protein
entries.anchor: Results, 'Wwox Loss Reduces E-Cadherin, ERK, and p63 Expression in Keratinocytes'

entries.proposition: THE PAPER'S OWN STATEMENT OF CONTEXT-DEPENDENCE, which is the general principle the dose question turns on and which this paper states more plainly than any other source in the batch.
entries.snippet: the control of cell growth and apoptosis by WWOX may depend on cell types, such as their tissue origin, differentiation state or differences between normal, benign and malignant cells

entries.proposition: A SECOND, INDEPENDENT INSTANCE OF RAISED WWOX DOING THE OPPOSITE OF THE TUMOUR-SUPPRESSOR EXPECTATION -- reported here as a citation to Nowakowska 2014, NOT measured by these authors. It is carried as a pointer to an unread source, not as a datum.
entries.snippet: in low-grade invasive HT29 colon adenocarcinoma cells, increased WWOX expression promotes cell proliferation but inhibits apoptosis
entries.anchor: Discussion, same paragraph, citing Nowakowska et al. 2014

entries.proposition: AND THE AUTHORS DRAW THE TWO-SIDED CONCLUSION EXPLICITLY. Written in 2020, independently of the 2026 preprint, it is the same proposition: the quantity matters in both directions.
entries.snippet: A certain amount of WWOX expression may be necessary for maintaining normal physiological functions in cells.
entries.anchor: Discussion, paragraph on pleiotropic functions, sentence following the cell-type dependence sentence

entries.proposition: This paper performs no overexpression experiment of its own: the raised-WWOX proposition it is cited for is a statement about other people's experiments.
entries.snippet: In contrast, in low-grade invasive HT29 colon adenocarcinoma cells, increased WWOX expression promotes cell proliferation but inhibits apoptosis

entries.proposition: The epidermal barrier is not measurably impaired even in the homozygous null, and the exact P value is printed on the panel and in no legend.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 1A plots transepidermal water loss in g/h m2 at P21 for Wwox+/+, Wwox+/- and Wwox-/- mice with the string P=0.3894 printed above the plot; the group means read approximately 6.2, 5.9 and 4.3 and the point counts are 8, 9 and 5. The figure legend states the test but no P value.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Figure 1, panel A; supplementary image inspected at native resolution

entries.proposition: Hair-follicle development up to E18.5 is a clean null across all three genotypes, with both exact P values printed on the panels and in no legend.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 6 panel A plots hair-follicle number per mm at E16.5 for Wwox+/+, Wwox+/- and Wwox-/- with the string P=0.56 printed above it, and panel B plots hair-follicle length in micrometres at E18.5 for the same three genotypes with the string P=0.62 printed above it. The legend gives neither value.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Figure 6, panels A and B; supplementary image inspected at native resolution

entries.proposition: The heterozygote is indistinguishable from wild type on the quantified apoptosis endpoint while the homozygous null is raised, and the missing bracket is a tested null under the legend's all-pairwise test.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Supplementary Figure 4B plots TUNEL-positive epidermal cells as a percentage at P21 for Wwox+/+, Wwox+/- and Wwox-/- at approximately 0.8, 0.85 and 1.8 with five points per group. Significance brackets are drawn for Wwox+/+ versus Wwox-/- marked * and for Wwox+/- versus Wwox-/- marked *, and no bracket is drawn between Wwox+/+ and Wwox+/-. The legend states one-way ANOVA and post hoc Tukey tests with n=5.
entries.anchor: Supplementary Figure 4, panel B; supplementary image inspected at native resolution
